programmes.d: The experts converge on Normanby Hall where treasures include a marble bust and a pair of rare candlesticks won in a newspaper competition.
A set of royal cufflinks; letter from Adm. Nelson; collection of silver found in the back of a church's safe.
Inside the Pannier Market the team discover a cache of curiosities including an inmate's uniform from the early days of Dartmoor prison and a valuable plate bought for a song at a boot sale.
Michael Aspel traces what happened to some of the items featured on the show; preview of a new program.
Michael Aspel digs up unscreened finds from recent Roadshows. Amongst the objects are a ring once owned by the Romanian Royal family, an elaborate bed and a bizarre collection of coffinalia.
A small statue thought to be from King Tut's tomb; Punch & Judy set; sword pistol.
The team head east to Ipswich where they discover a Duke's chamber pot now used to drink champagne and one of the earliest record players.
A bust of Dylan Thomas; book of early silhouettes; plate.
The team step back in time at the Beamish Open Air Museum. Amongst the items are a rare rapier sword allegedly smuggled out of Russia in the props box of the Bolshoi Ballet.
An early Mickey Mouse mascot; a rare deco figurine; documents that once belonged to the bodyguard of the Duke and Duchess of Windsor.
The team enter Border country as the Roadshow visits Manderston. Amongst the items are pieces from Queen Victoria's household, a gruesome Man Trap and Lord Palmer's collection of biscuit tins.
Marble bust; a pair of rare candlesticks; a man collects and races antique lawnmowers.
Amongst the objects under scrutiny in Rochdale's magnificent town hall are a gold pencil gifted by King George IV, paint brushes used by LS Lowry and the diaries of a British hangman.
Pannier Market in Tavistock, Devon.
The team visits the Royal Hospital in Chelsea. Amongst the items are a Roulette table built to outwit cheats, a collection of buttons worn by Charles Dickens and a gilded bee from a royal throne.
Finds from Lichfield and Normanby include a ring once owned by the Romanian royal family, an Arts and Crafts bed, and a collection of coffinalia.
The team are at the seaside resort of Ventnor. Under scrutiny is a family portrait showing a Speaker of the House of Commons as a young boy and 75 Austin vehicles.
Duke's chamber pot now used to drink champagne; early record player.
Michael Aspel introduces a selection of unscreened finds. Items include an Edward VIII Coronation souvenir that was hastily converted to an abdication mug and early fan mail for Elton John.
At Beamish Open Air Museum, items include a rare rapier, battlefield finds, and a music box.
The Roadshow team head for Lancaster. Amongst the items uncovered in the Town Hall are a valuable pair of clogs, a moving series of letters from Crimea, an anti-slavery ring and a rare tapestry.
A visit to Manderston, near Berwick on Tweed, features pieces from Queen Victoria's household.
At Coughton Court in Warwickshire, the team finds original designs from one of Britain's leading graphic artists, a bizarre Japanese depiction of skeletons dancing and a lost masterpiece.
Amongst the objects in Rochdale are a gold pencil and paint brushes used by LS Lowry.
Back at Coughton Court, the experts get excited about an Agatha Christie letter, a medal awarded to those who came to the aid of the Titanic survivors and a rare figure of the Queen on horseback.
Michael Aspel and the team visit the Royal Hospital in Chelsea and discover items like a roulette table built to outwit cheats valued at $45,000 and a collection of buttons worn by Charles Dickens.
The team visits Sydney, Australia. Under scrutiny are pieces of furniture made by convicts, a part of the keel of Captain Cook's ship, and one collector receives one of the show's biggest valuations.
Among the objects under scrutiny at the seaside resort of Ventnor on the Isle of Wight are a family portrait showing the future Speaker of the House of Commons as a young boy.
The team heads to the Cathedral cloisters in Norwich. Amongst the items are a letter from Lord Nelson, a series of portraits, and correspondence from John Lennon's Aunt Mimi.

We revisit the cloisters of Norwich Cathedral. The team uncovers original illustrations from Black Beauty and a rare saucer used for many years as an ashtray.
Pair of clogs; series of letters from the Crimea; intricately woven tapestry.
Michael Aspel and the team travel to Londonderry. Under scrutiny are the most intricately produced hand cut pictures to appear on the program, a cache of silver and a cushion woven from human hair.

Michael Aspel introduces unscreened finds including a pair of figures that narrowly escaped a bombing raid, a recipe book with hair raising potions and a painting by one of Queen Victoria's children.
Michael Aspel and the team head for Coughton Court in Warwickshire, where the experts get excited about an Agatha Christie letter and a rare china figure of the queen on horseback.
Michael Aspel and the experts set up camp in Somerset. Amongst the items are a set of chairs that witnessed the battle of Trafalgar and a valuable postcard collection.
Furniture made by convicts; keel of Capt. Cook's ship; items that belonged to Maria Callas.
In Somerset, Michael Aspel and the team discover one of the rarest pieces of silver ever found on the Roadshow, a car powered by steam, and a set of original illustrations for Winnie the Pooh.
Letter from Lord Nelson; portraits depicting ancestors of Walt Disney; correspondence from John Lennon's Aunt Mimi.
In the Royal Exhibition Building, in Melbourne, Australia, Michael Aspel and the team uncover relics from the days of gold strikes, a flag flown at the battle of Trafalgar and a sad looking bear.

Pair of bisque figures; early recipe book with potions and lotions; painting by one of Queen Victoria's children.
